Thanks Dylan — looping in Contracts. Quick notes from my side after a first pass of the attachments:
- We have an internal Exhibit D template that covers data flows and access controls; I can map NovumTech's diagram to that template but will need clarification on whether logs/telemetry include PII. If yes, we'll route to privacy for a stricter retention baseline.
- For residency: we can support customer-managed residency (EU) for stored artifacts tied to the customer account. Need to confirm whether KV cache or ephemeral inference state must be stored persistently — that changes the scope.
- Billing cadence: we generally invoice monthly for hosted usage; for pilots we can do a net-30 trial invoice or include in the order form as a one-time prepay credit. Please confirm preference.

Can someone confirm the technical residency requirement in plain language (temporary cache vs persisted storage)? If NovumTech wants persisted storage in EU, we will need to scope Dedicated or Private deployment options in the order form.

I'll prepare a redline priority list: mandatory security/privacy carveouts, residency clause, and signature matrix. Attaching my checklist as inline comments in the contract once we have the clarified asks.

Thanks — flagged a few legal points for prioritization. High-level guidance for redlines (so Sales knows negotiation levers):
1) Data residency: we can offer EU residency for stored customer inputs and logs at contract signature. If NovumTech requires residency for ephemeral KV cache that is only present during inference, that's a more operational ask and may require Dedicated/Private. We should propose residency for persisted artifacts and document the architecture in Exhibit D.
2) IP / Model outputs: propose standard Redwood language — customer retains ownership of their inputs and outputs; Redwood retains model weights and improvements. If NovumTech insists on derivative/training restrictions, we can add a narrow no‑training clause for the customer's data during the pilot period.
3) Logs & telemetry retention: default 90 days; can offer 30/365 as an option in Order Form pricing.
4) Indemnity and limitation caps: keep standard template caps; if NovumTech wants higher caps limit, escalate to Sales leadership for approval.

Also drafting a starter redline bundle: (A) Exhibit D mapping & retention table, (B) Residency addendum, (C) Pilot billing and credits language. Kimberly — I'll drop a tracked-redline MSA in the shared Drive link below when ready.

Thanks all — appreciate the quick responses. A few clarifications from NovumTech's procurement and security leads:
- Residency: we require persisted storage of customer inputs and model logs in the EU region for the pilot. Ephemeral cache during runtime is acceptable if not persisted.
- PII: event logs may contain user identifiers; we will scrub or pseudonymize where possible but we need retention to be capped at 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Signers: procurement will countersign; legal will route. Targeting signature by 2026-08-15.
- Billing: prefer pilot as a one-time prepaid credit applied to first invoice; net-30 acceptable if Redwood needs that.

I uploaded a slightly cleaned-up diagram and the procurement contact sheet to our shared link. If we can get the starter redlines by end of week (Jul 23) that would keep our mid-August target alive.
